newsitem.title: USA: White House monitoring tobacco settlement talks.
newsitem.headline: White House monitoring tobacco settlement talks.

text.p: The White House on Wednesday said it was monitoring talks between two of the nation's largest cigarette makers and plantiffs negotiating a settlement, but stressed it was not a direct participant.
"We are closely monitoring the negotiations," White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry said.

He said that Philip Morris Cos. Inc. Chairman Geoffrey Bible and RJR Nabisco Corp. Chairman Steven Goldstone had attended the beginning of talks and other tobacco executives remain at the bargaining table.

The parties are discussing the establishment of a $300 billion fund to pay for smoking-related injuries over a 25-year period, the source said, adding that this is just the beginning of talks and other negotiating sessions are expected in the future.

In Washington, the White House said it was monitoring the talks but stressed that it was not a direct participant. "We are closely monitoring the negotiations," White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry said.
